A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KANO research, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. v3 retains the material in Appendices A–C and adds Appendices D–E; the substantial revision does not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-operator experiments and quantum-dynamics simulations, including generalization losses, recovered symbolic coefficients, and state infidelities in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds evaluated baselines and MLP ablation results in Tables 1 and 3.

M1.justification: The principal KANO architecture and Q-KANO propagation equations remain unchanged. v3 introduces KANO_MLP and Q-KANO_MLP ablation variants that replace KAN subnetworks with MLPs, constituting limited architectural adaptations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three synthetic operators, six training/testing function families, and double-well and nonlinear Schrödinger dynamics under the same supervision scenarios. The additional experiments vary models rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The synthetic comparison expands from FNO and KANO variants to include U-FNO, AM-FNO, PDNO, and KANO_MLP in Table 1. Table 3 additionally evaluates Q-KANO_MLP under position-and-momentum supervision. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 explicitly adds the B/A loss ratio as a generalization summary and specifies two-layer, approximately size-matched additional baselines and an MLP ablation with width 32 and two hidden layers. Existing protocols remain unchanged; Appendix B.1 still specifies 2,000 training samples and 400 test samples from each group despite the shorter main-text description.

E4.justification: v3 adds KAN-versus-MLP component ablations across the synthetic operators and quantum benchmarks, testing whether generalization depends on KAN subnetworks or the dual-domain architecture. This supplies substantial new evidence about the architecture's contribution; the earlier interpolation and symbolic-recovery analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-run counts, specified seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The reporting remains point estimates and curves without uncertainty bands; the six figure images are unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing result values and recovered coefficients in Tables 1–4 are retained, while v3 adds substantial baseline and ablation results. For example, KANO_MLP has Group B losses of 6.59, 8.07, and 6.87 in units of 10^-4; Q-KANO_MLP has double-well/NLSE infidelities of 7.7×10^-6 and 8.5×10^-6. These are additional results, not improvements to retained model scores.

T1.justification: The original lemmas, theorems, and Appendix C proofs are substantively retained. New Appendix D adds Proposition 1 and higher-order Fréchet-derivative and multilayer spectral-coupling arguments. Appendix E adds formal FLOP, memory, and accuracy-dependent complexity derivations, substantially expanding the theoretical content.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the principal expressivity, generalization, symbolic-recovery, and numerical-performance claims. However, v1's explicit claim to be the first work demonstrating and quantifying symbolic operator recovery through KAN is absent from v3, along with its introductory contribution statement.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the MLP ablations as evidence that dual-domain structure drives generalization. It newly discusses unresolved lift/projection-network effects, high-dimensional applications as future work, KANO's higher computational cost, and regimes favoring FNO. Some new interpretation overreaches: describing U-FNO as worse overlooks its smaller B/A ratios than FNO on G1 and G3.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the additional baselines' approximate parameter counts and layer configuration, plus the MLP ablation's hidden width and depth. Appendix B's data-generation and simulation instructions are unchanged. Neither PDF supplies code-access information, hardware specifications, or a detailed training budget.

R1.justification: Removing the original introduction eliminates substantial positioning against DeepOKAN, KAN-ODEs, EFKAN, and several FNO extensions. v3 adds literature on operator universality and lower bounds, KAN symbolic-recovery limitations, irregular-function representations, and high-dimensional applications, substantially changing the research context.

P1.justification: v1's motivation, related-work synthesis, and contribution narrative are replaced by Introduction subsections 1.1–1.2 that largely duplicate Background subsections 2.1–2.2. Together with expanded experimental discussion and new explanatory remarks, this substantially changes the narrative structure and introduces conspicuous repetition.

P2.justification: Table 1 becomes a full-width comparison with additional rows and B/A columns, and Table 3 gains an ablation row. Several existing figures and tables are repositioned. All six figure images remain identical, so the display changes are concentrated in table structure and placement.

improvement.justification: The added baselines and MLP ablations strengthen empirical support, and the scope and computational caveats are useful. However, v3 loses the original introductory framing and duplicates background material. Its new efficiency argument also contains an inconsistency between polynomial parameter scaling in Equation 53 and the exponential expression in Equation 54, while comparing lower bounds does not establish computational superiority. These material benefits and defects leave the net quality direction uncertain.
